Actual Article Body:
The far-left candidate for Michigan Senate attacked Trump this week for ‘interfering with the freedom of the press.’

The Democrats’ Islamist communist candidate for Senate in swing state Michigan earlier this week snidely criticized President Donald Trump’s decision to take away White House passes from leftist propaganda outlets — MS Now, CNN, and Politico.

“May I just say, it’s nice to see MSNow and CNN covering the news,” Abdul El-Sayed, the Eddie Haskell of Muslim politicians, told reporters during a campaign stop with the Democratic Party’s failed replacement presidential candidate, Kamala Harris. “That’s what you do, it’s great.”

“You are welcome here anytime to cover news. I’m grateful that you do that. I mean, there are certain people who occupy certain offices that are too cowardly to take your questions,” the smarmy public health bureaucrat and failed former candidate for governor added in a not-so-subtle jab at the president.

He was more direct in another exchange with the media, asserting that “Trump hates the idea of democracy.”

“That’s why he denies elections and is interfering with the freedom of the press,” El-Sayed told Deadline Detroit.

That’s an interesting criticism from a guy who reportedly once urged the Muslim Brotherhood to “purge” news outlets and law enforcement in Egypt. The Trump administration has designated the Muslim Brotherhood a terrorist organization.

As The Washington Free Beacon reported on Wednesday, the “demand was made in an Arabic-language statement on Al-Ahram Gate, an Egyptian news portal.” It was signed by 46 “leaders of the Egyptian community” living in the U.S., “one of whom was El-Sayed, who was born in Michigan to Egyptian immigrants.”

“We, leaders of the Egyptian community, support the revolutionary decisions taken by the president, and we call on him to purge the media and the police as quickly as possible,” states the letter published in 2012 after Islamist Mohamed Morsi, who was Egypt’s president at the time, grabbed sweeping powers to quell growing unrest.

Laura Loomer first reported on the declaration in April.

Abdul El-Sayed signed on to an Arabic-language statement in 2012 demanding that the Muslim Brotherhood “purge” media and police in Egypt. The repressive Islamic group carried out a brutal religious crackdown on the press soon thereafter, @LevineJonathan reports. pic.twitter.com/LMHTzBfGua

The Free Beacon noted that the letter remains online, but the link appears to have been removed. As of late Wednesday, the link produced an error message. Loomer, however, included the letter in her original post.

It appears the signers of the declaration got their wish. Morsi and his “brothers” cracked down on critics, harassing and suppressing journalists. Some stood trial, others were attacked in the street, according to media accounts at the time. Some were targeted for the crime of “insulting Islam.”

“This is a troubling backward step that Egypt’s newly elected President Mohamed Morsi should not be taking,” Robert Mahoney, Deputy Director of the Committee to Protect Journalists, said in an Aug. 16, 2012 report. “We urge President Morsi to reverse this course immediately and demonstrate his commitment to press freedom.”

El-Sayed wrote in support of the Muslim Brotherhood before the group rode Morsi to power.  In a HuffPost op-ed amid the mass protests of the so-called Egyptian Spring, the Islamist argued that the U.S. had nothing to fear from the group that would ultimately be designated a terrorist group by the U.S.

Revoking the White House press credentials of three propaganda-pushing corporate media outlets is hardly the journalism “purge” that El-Sayed signed on to. In the first place, MS Now, CNN, and Politico have the right of redress. They are exercising it, almost immediately filing a lawsuit on First Amendment grounds. Egyptian journalists didn’t enjoy the same protection then — or now.
